status: DRAFT — public consultation CP/N26/2, not in force
source: Projet de règlement ILR/N26/X portant sur les modalités de notification et les critères des incidents ayant un impact important (NISS)
legal_basis: Loi du 5 mai 2026 concernant des mesures destinées à assurer un niveau élevé de cybersécurité, art. 14 (1) et (3)

notification_channel.automated: other automated means agreed in advance with the Institut
notification_channel.note: Art. 1(2) — the same channel must be used for all subsequent actions on the same incident.

scope.applies_to: essential and important entities (entités essentielles et importantes)
scope.excluded: entities covered by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 — Art. 2(6)
scope.note: IR 2024/2690 entity types keep their EU thresholds; this regulation does not displace them.

replaces.description: Art. 5 abrogates the NIS1-era sector regulations. CyberScale implements nine of these eleven.

abrogated.subject: réseaux et services de communications électroniques

significant_incident_criteria.description: Art. 2(1) — twelve criteria. Any one triggers notification. Unlike the abrogated regulations these are generic: there are no per-sector thresholds in the body of the text.

a_service_disruption.description: Service partially or totally inaccessible or unavailable for more than one hour, OR affecting more than 5% of the users of that service in Luxembourg
a_service_disruption.condition: service_impact in (degraded, unavailable, sustained) AND (impact_duration_hours > 1 OR users_affected_pct_lu > 5)
a_service_disruption.note: Partial inaccessibility counts — 'partiellement ou totalement'. The two limbs are alternatives, not cumulative.

b_malicious_unauthorised_access.description: Effective unauthorised access to network and information systems, suspected malicious, and liable to cause serious operational disruption
b_malicious_unauthorised_access.condition: suspected_malicious AND data_impact in (accessed, compromised, exfiltrated, systemic) AND liable_serious_disruption
b_malicious_unauthorised_access.note: 'Susceptible de causer une perturbation opérationnelle grave' is a forward-looking judgement, not an observed state.

c_cia_impact_50_users.description: Impact on authenticity, integrity or confidentiality of networks, services, or stored/processed/transmitted data, affecting more than 50 users in Luxembourg

d_trade_secret_exfiltration.description: Exfiltration of trade secrets within the meaning of art. 2 point 1° of the loi du 26 juin 2019

e_cross_border.description: Cross-border or international impact, actual or liable

f_physical_access_compromised.description: Physical access to the infrastructure used to provide a service is compromised

g_public_safety_risk.description: Risk to public safety, security or health, actual or liable
g_public_safety_risk.condition: public_safety_risk is true OR safety_impact in (health_damage, death)

h_health_damage_person.description: Considerable damage to the health of a natural person, actual or liable

i_death.description: Death of a natural person, actual or liable

j_direct_financial_loss.description: Direct financial loss of at least EUR 500 000 or at least 5% of the entity's total annual turnover, whichever is the lower
j_direct_financial_loss.note: 'Le montant le plus faible étant retenu' — the threshold is the LOWER of the two, so a small entity's 5% can bind well below EUR 500 000.

k_prejudice_to_persons.description: Material or moral prejudice of at least EUR 50 000 to a legal person, or at least EUR 10 000 to a natural person

l_annex_criteria.description: Criteria defined in the annexes to the regulation, which may add sector-, entity-type- or entity-group-specific thresholds
l_annex_criteria.condition: not evaluable — annexes not published with the consultation draft
l_annex_criteria.note: This is the route by which sector-specific thresholds could return. The consultation PDF contains no annexes, so their content is unknown.

scheduled_maintenance.description: Planned service interruptions and the foreseen consequences of scheduled maintenance carried out by or for the entity are not important incidents

incident_duration.description: Period from disruption of service delivery in terms of availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality until its restoration
incident_duration.note: Duration is not availability-only: an integrity or confidentiality disruption also starts the clock.

recurrence_rule.description: Incidents that are individually below threshold are collectively an important incident when ALL three conditions hold
conditions: occurred at least twice within six months
share the same apparent root cause
collectively meet criterion (j) — direct financial loss
recurrence_rule.note: Requires incident history across a six-month window. CyberScale assesses one incident at a time and holds no such state.

content: estimate of the number of users potentially concerned
suspicion of an illicit or malicious act
initial assessment of severity and impact

trust_service_provider_derogation.note: Trust service providers notify within 24 hours, not 72, for incidents affecting their trust services.

content: date the incident began, if known
whether availability, integrity, confidentiality or authenticity was affected
any further information requested by the Institut

de_notification.description: If internal analysis later shows the incident meets none of the criteria, the declarant shares that conclusion with the Institut without delay

media_disclosure.description: The entity shares with the Institut any information it discloses to the media about an important incident; where an incident is publicised independently of the entity, it informs the Institut as to the veracity of the facts
